title: Metaphor Tree
description: A hierarchical structure representing a story as interconnected metaphors. The tree is a gradient from abstract (root) to concrete (leaves). Schema is flexible—not all fields are required for every story.

root.description: The most abstract node—the core movement/transformation

core_movement.description: The fundamental emotional/thematic transformation (e.g., 'trapped → free', 'innocent → corrupted')

target_effect.description: What change we want in the audience (optional but recommended)

nodes.description: All nodes in the tree, each referencing its parent. First level below root is most abstract; deepest levels are most concrete (scenes).

depth.description: How many levels deep the tree goes

node.description: A node in the metaphor tree. More abstract near root, more concrete toward leaves.

parent_id.description: ID of parent node (null for nodes directly under root)

content.description: What this node represents—description scales with concreteness

abstraction_level.description: Where on the gradient this sits (e.g., 'pattern', 'archetype', 'character', 'scene', 'beat')

weight.description: Metaphorical weight—how central to the theme

function.description: What role this plays in the story/core movement

resonance.description: How this connects to its parent—why this concrete choice embodies the abstract

monomyth_role.description: Optional: which Hero's Journey beat this serves (ordinary_world, catalyst, ordeal, etc.)

echo.description: How this echoes or foreshadows other parts of the story

children_hint.description: Guidance for what kind of children this node might have
